english: Welcome to my pad. Go ahead. Root around as much as you want.
Oh. So I can have some of your stuff?
Thank you for letting me in.
I won't touch anything. I'll just look. Intensely.
He sighs. "I'm not sure how this is in any way useful for the job."
But let me know when you're done looking around.
I'll chill here for a bit.
How long have you lived here?
I don't spend much time here.
I don't know. Three years? Four?
Gods, has it been that long...?
Real cheap. But I got a special deal because of the HWBT gig.
That's real good for such a fancy apartment.
The Old Lady takes care of her own, eh?
It's central. Right next to the Garden.
That's all I really care about. Although the ventilation system is pretty sweet during those colder months.
Mm, he mouths and gives you a side glance.
Time to dance around the subject.
I could tell him the truth...
It's really the only good choice here.
Yes! Right away! Before he notices something's off!
A lie? Hm. But that might make him dislike you...
The truth is freedom. Honor. Goodness.
Although... perhaps you can make an exception.
There's absolutely nothing wrong with your current living arrangements.
And the goblin will not think lesser of you because of it.
Guess clerics are well taken care of, huh?
We sure are. We sure... are.
I remember now. You live with your mom.
It's honorable. Traditional family housing is good for society.
Well I guess that's... not too uncommon.
He does not mean harm. Yet... it hurts.
He tries to not linger on the subject, since he sees your pain.
I can't afford my own place.
She's not home a lot. So I mostly have it to myself.
I used to live in the Towers, but they kicked me out.
Mm. The economy is shit, I agree.
Oh. That also makes it more... understandable.
I don't mean to get all personal, but if I had to live with my mother I'd probably end up like one of those energy zombies.
Explains why he's so against the idea of generational housing.
Can I... can I ask why?
Look, they just had some problems with some of my writing.
Maybe we can... talk about something else.
What, can't be that bad at spelling, eh?
Spelling. Hah. Because you're a cleric. Casting spells.
The unofficial mark of a traitor.

I got a new patriarch who didn't like me, and then when I presented an argument for a republican revolution without the influence of the Free Cities, they said it was a 'misuse of state resources', and they branded me with a minor case of <shake>dereliction</shake>. Really, it's all overblown, and Bjôrn uses the same copper press all the time for a bunch of personal stuff and he never gets in trouble over it so it just seems really overblown to me and yeah.
(Look away and steer the conversation to something else.)
He listens to your rant with an intense interest.
So they can just do that? Toss you out?
I don't think they like me very much.
But you're still employed as a Cleric?
Of course. This was just a disciplinary action. They've been mad at me since I refused to register as a member of the Party of Norvik.
Interesting. So this whole thing is sort of like a redemption run for you then?
Solving the mystery of the tea shop that exploded, and so on. Rejoin the fold.
Yes. Redemption is within grasp. Then I'll jump right onto the Party, and remake it in my image.
No. Fuck them. They're all going to get thrown out when the Freestriders take over.
It doesn't matter. Once the election is over, I'll go back to doing Azgalist activism, like in the good old days.
I'll solve it to prove my abilities. Eventually I'll lead the city myself.
I don't care anymore. I'll go be an agrarian or something.
He lets out a big laugh.
Truest thing you've said all day.
...You sure have had a lot of political aspirations, haven't you?
He gives you a slow nod.
As a Magocrat or just a general clerical dictator?
As per usual: good luck with that.
He wants you to speak. Ugh.
Eh. Just tell him. Why not?
Being a Cleric must be hard.
Not so bad. Thanks to the Old Lady.
Not every goblin is so lucky.
Yeah, I've noticed that you've got it pretty nice here.
You're lucky to be living in Norvik, you mean.
You know there are three tribes in the city, right?
The Halfways get by real well, thanks to Lady Sageleaf.
But it didn't used to be that way. And most goblins have a real hard time getting by here.
Most guilds won't exactly hire a goblin just like that.
I see. They must not want goblins due to the gobliny nature of them. I mean, you guys.
He gives you the stink eye.
We're not human. So by default - on average - we're not trusted.

Back in the day, there were apparently a bunch of programs meant to push us into the work force. Anti-discrimination laws. Goblin-public works projects. But the support for those ran out way before I was born.
So most kids just fall into crime.
They can't do that. In Norvik it's illegal to be a criminal.
They need to try harder. Crime is the easy way.
That's understandable. It's the only path for them.
Arguably one of the dumbest things you've ever said.
You clearly haven't heard everything I've ever said.
Dumbest thing so far. (Hold up a finger.)
No. It's the only way for most of them.
Imagine you're a goblin kid. You spend most your day in the warren, with twenty others your age.

There's barely any resources to actually teach you all the human stuff we're legally forced to be taught. If you're lucky you've got one parent with a stable income. Otherwise you'll be living in the dormitories.
No support system. No chance to integrate into this 'city' you're supposed to be living in.

If you're lucky, you'll get a dangerous gig in the tunnels. If not, the only way for you to get enough money for food, beyond the basic handouts, is joining a syndicate. They recruit young, to keep you in the juvenile-stockade if you get caught. Starting as an errand-boy. Ending up as... whatever they need for their enterprises.
Then you bring home a heavy pouch of crowns for your mom and pops. What are they gonna do? Turn their little kid in? Or accept the only major income the household's gotten in months?
Maybe they'll even encourage you. Push you to get real friendly with the local runner.
But it's not like this in the Halfways?
The Halfway Bridge Tribe is classified as a syndicate. We run things in a similar sense to the Ishkii and the NMBT. Except we do things strictly by the book. We don't run drugs, for one.
If you ignore a certain bird... then we've keep Waterlane free of smuggling for years at this point.
We keep Waterlane free of smuggling.

But most importantly, we keep the youth out of it. And we keep the other tribes at an arm's length. Lady Sageleaf is real draconian in that regard. Everyone, and I mean everyone in our tribe gets a job and a good salary.
We've tried pushing this method, our support system, onto the other tribes, but it's hard. And not always popular. We're the... small annoying cultish tribe of Tolstad, after all.
He sighs. Again. "So it is what it is."
Seems to be no difference when it comes to the solution: a purpose and a place. That's all they need.
You're working hard for your Lady.
You catch him glancing at the image of her on the board.
Maybe I did, maybe I didn't.
He rubs his eyes and lets out a deep groan.
Why is this how I spend my days?
I don't think I even want to ask what you mean by that.
Gobliny means... dirty. Muddy. Barbaric, I guess?
I don't mean it in a bad way.
Okay, you're just gonna tell me anyway. Great.
Oh? What kind of way do you mean it, then?
In the neutral way. I don't have strong opinions about anything.
In a 'you surprise me with your civilized behavior' kind of way.
His voice is dripping with genuine gratefulness.
I don't know if that's better or worse, he mutters.
Thanks. You also surprise me. All the time.
Thanks, brother. (Give him a fist bump.)
You mean that in a good or bad way?
Let me think about it for three to five seconds before I answer.
He stands there and stares at you.
Is this how long you take before answering every single time?
It's painful. You should try to be quicker.
I mean it in a good way, he eventually tells you.
Now- you ready to head out yet?
Or do you want to shuffle around my goblin-hole for a bit longer?
You catch him cringing over his own phrasing.
He leans on the couch, wearing a tired face.
Yeah. I'm not here a lot.
I'd argue it's much better than usual. One time, I was on a date- brought her back here.

Terrible idea. The date was already going poorly. Imagine her expression when she steps in here, and there's a pile of reports all over the floor, a blocked drain in the kitchen sink, and fifteen confiscated bowls of pixie dust piled in the corner.
Let me tell you- took her ten seconds to come up with an excuse!
He recounts the tale with excellent timing.
This is one of his favorites. He tells this one to everyone.

As his laughter fades, he looks around the place and tells you, "Ah. Anyway. Looks better these days. Figured if I'm such a 'neat' goblin like everyone says, I might as well keep my apartment clean too."
I have a hard time believing you. Snell, living in filth? Never.
Back when I was still looking for that sort of thing.
You know. Getting tied down, so on.
Eh. I've made peace with it.
I don't think people change. But I do believe that all folk can control their behavior.
They sure do. Time changes all things.
I don't. I'm the exact same person I've always been, flaws and all.
No need to get all deep with it.
I don't know if it's a cleric thing, or not, but you could probably land a nice gal or guy if you wanted.
He does not care about your lack of experience.
Don't blame you though. Cleric work must be real hard work.
The question cuts tiny little holes in your inside-skull.
He is NOT allowed to ask you personal things like that.
The goblin looks at you, with no particular expression on his face.
He's expecting an answer, so you're going to have to give one.
Not a lie though- you can't handle that right now.
Just keep it simple. Dismiss the question in a nice way.
Nothing lately. I'm busy with work. (Be cool.)
You seem like the type to be busy with work too.
What? But... won't that be weird?
You're shivering in front of him, just from him asking a simple question.
I would rather talk about something else.
We have GREAT weather these days.
(Start screaming, then speak.) "Ahh- the anuran are interesting creatures. Have you ever met an anuran? Lovely frog-folk."
Snell stares at you for approximately six seconds.
He'll allow you to move on. Phew!
...Nevermind. Do you have something else to say about your life?
For the last few years I've just been focused on the Halfways. And whatever the Old Lady needs of me.
Don't mean to sound ungrateful though. I do love it. It's real rewarding.
What kind of reward? Like... treasure?
You seem more like a servant.
You're clearly good at what you do. Whatever that is.
Not that far off, even if it hurts my <u>ego</u> a bit when you put it like that.
I ask myself that same question sometimes.
I'd tell you to look at it from a goblin-perspective, but...
Let me put it like this. Lady Sageleaf gave me options in a world of railroad tracks. I get to help my people and get real fucking good at it.
So for now, I'm going to keep doing it.
But you at least get a good salary, right?
Maybe you should try something else later.
This definitely is not the type of job that ever leaves you bored.
Like I'm trying to tell you: goblins don't have too many options in this city.
Maybe I'll turn out real good at magic, and become the first goblin cleric.
You feel attuned with the esoteric?
That sounds like a terrible idea.
The goblin is very clearly not talented in anything magical.
He is clearly, and obviously joking.
Anyhow. Anything else you wanna chat about, or can we get going?
